purpose: Authority-to-Remedy Trace educational source registry. Verify applicable effective date and subsequent law before real filing.

sources.title: Declaration of Independence: historical principle, not legally binding
sources.summary: Consent of the governed is a historical principle. The Declaration itself is not a standalone source of judicially enforceable claims.

sources.title: United States Constitution: Articles I, II, III and VI
sources.summary: Separate legislative, executive and judicial powers; federal courts need jurisdiction; supremacy is not a general agency chain of command over state courts.

sources.title: Bill of Rights: First, Fifth, Ninth and Tenth Amendments
sources.summary: Petition, due process, retained rights and reserved powers. Individual disagreement does not remove lawful jurisdiction.

sources.title: Fourteenth Amendment, Section 1
sources.summary: State action is constrained by due process and equal protection.

sources.title: Florida Constitution, Articles I and V
sources.summary: Art I §1: political power inherent in people; §9: due process; §21: courts/access remedy; Art V allocates judicial power.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §551
sources.summary: Federal agency and agency-action definitions. Agency action includes failure to act; courts are excluded from agency definition.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §553
sources.summary: Rulemaking framework; §553(e) gives interested persons the right to petition for issuance, amendment or repeal of a rule. It does not compel adoption of desired rule.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §555
sources.summary: §555(b): conclude matters within reasonable time; §555(e): prompt denial notice for qualifying written requests, brief reasons subject to listed exceptions.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §701
sources.summary: Review exclusions: statutory preclusion, action committed to discretion. Federal agency definition excludes U.S. courts and does not cover Florida dependency courts.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §702
sources.summary: Review for a person suffering legal wrong or adversely affected within meaning of a relevant statute; waiver concerns relief other than money damages and has limits.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §704
sources.summary: Statutorily reviewable action and final action without another adequate court remedy; examine special review statutes and legally required administrative appeals. Inaction claims require separate analysis.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. §706
sources.summary: §706(1) unlawfully withheld/unreasonably delayed action; §706(2) grounds for review of action; record and prejudicial-error considerations.

sources.title: Norton v. Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance, 542 U.S. 55 (2004)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court opinion, Library of Congress
sources.summary: A §706(1) claim requires discrete agency action legally required. Broad programmatic demands are insufficient; duty to decide does not necessarily dictate outcome.

sources.title: 28 U.S.C. §1331
sources.summary: Federal-question original jurisdiction. Cause of action, jurisdiction, waiver and venue are separate inquiries.

sources.title: 28 U.S.C. §1361
sources.summary: District courts have jurisdiction of an action in the nature of mandamus to compel a federal officer/employee/agency duty owed to plaintiff; availability requires further doctrinal analysis.

sources.title: 42 U.S.C. §1983
sources.summary: Remedy for deprivation of federal rights under color of state law, subject to requirements and defenses; limits injunctive relief against judicial officers. It is not a general state-court appellate vehicle.

sources.title: Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555 (1992)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court opinion, Library of Congress
sources.summary: Article III standing requires injury, traceability and redressability; generalized disapproval of government is insufficient.

sources.title: Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Saudi Basic Industries Corp., 544 U.S. 280 (2005)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court opinion, Library of Congress
sources.summary: Federal district courts do not serve as general appellate courts for state judgments; Rooker-Feldman is narrow and independent claims require separate analysis.

sources.title: Mireles v. Waco, 502 U.S. 9 (1991)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court opinion, Library of Congress
sources.summary: Judicial immunity generally protects judicial acts from damages; nonjudicial acts and clear absence of all jurisdiction are distinct exceptions.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.013
sources.summary: Chapter39 circuit-court jurisdiction and counsel provisions; specialized jurisdiction rules still require checking.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.0132
sources.summary: Dependency proceeding records, confidentiality and authorized access.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.401
sources.summary: Taking into custody authority and predicates; distinguish removal from later adjudication.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.402
sources.summary: Shelter predicates, petition, notice, hearing and written-order findings; court order after hearing needed to hold in shelter longer than24 hours; exceptions and continuances require actual source check.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.407
sources.summary: Decision-specific medical/psychotropic authority; custody does not grant unlimited treatment authority. Branches distinguish consent, motion/report, objection/hearing, and emergencies.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.501
sources.summary: Dependency petition content and applicable filing timing; must not conflate shelter petition with dependency adjudication.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.506
sources.summary: Arraignment, notices and responses; procedural branch depends on appearance and response.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.507
sources.summary: Adjudicatory hearing, preponderance standard, corroboration of anonymous-call evidence, dismissal or dependency findings/order.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.510
sources.summary: Appeals of dependency orders; identify reviewability and current appellate rules.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.521
sources.summary: Disposition, family functioning assessment, case plan and required findings/next review. Section39.521(1)(a) has timing-dependent service branches; (1)(b) allows a court-found assessment exception; (1)(e) lists written-order contents.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §39.701
sources.summary: Review schedule, report and service, review of agency/parent performance. §(2)(d)3: after court finds agency noncompliance with written case plan, may contempt; shall order compliance plan and require showing why child cannot safely return.

sources.title: Florida Rules of Juvenile Procedure
sources.publisher: Florida Bar, official court rules compilation
sources.summary: Rules8.305 shelter;8.310 petition;8.315 arraignment;8.330 adjudication;8.340 disposition;8.345 postdisposition;8.415 review. Rule8.265 dependency rehearing does not toll appeal; (b)(4) requires rehearing to preserve missing-required-final-findings issue. Rule8.270 relief is distinct.

sources.title: Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure
sources.publisher: Florida Bar, official court rules compilation
sources.summary: Rule9.146 dependency appeals;9.110 final;9.130 specified nonfinal;9.100 extraordinary writ;9.020 rendition. Appeal is not generally automatic stay;9.146(c) contains TPR-specific provision.

sources.title: Second District Court of Appeal: geographic jurisdiction
sources.publisher: Florida Second District Court of Appeal
sources.summary: Second DCA includes Hillsborough County (13th Judicial Circuit). Florida Supreme Court review is jurisdiction-limited; federal district court is a separate branch.

sources.title: Fla. Stat. §934.03
sources.summary: Covered interception generally prohibited unless exception applies. §(2)(d) provides all-party prior consent route. Other exceptions and confidentiality/recording court rules require specific analysis.

sources.title: Eleventh Circuit: geographic jurisdiction
sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
sources.summary: The Eleventh Circuit covers federal cases from Alabama, Florida, and Georgia. Specific appellate jurisdiction still requires the applicable statute and rules.

sources.title: 28 U.S.C. §1257: Supreme Court review of state judgments
sources.summary: Qualifying final judgments from the highest state court in which a decision could be had may be reviewed by certiorari on the federal grounds specified by the statute; this is not automatic appellate review.
